thread: The newer grain seller (weak clue, mentioned twice, not connected)

evidence.clue: The girl, asked who came to the door in the last days: 'Gran Ottley, to sit with Mam. The newer grain seller. Da had words with Mam about him, because he was cheaper than Mister Hollis. The tinker, for the pot.' Jaina: 'What grain seller?' Girl: 'The new one.' Sylvanas turns it over once as ordinary: 'Every village south of the Pass had a new man with a cart once a season, and a husband and wife with words to say about him. She put it at the back of her head.'

The old carter at the bridge asks: 'You'll not have passed a young fellow on the road? Coming down from your way, with a grain cart. New man. I've a mind to see what he looks like.' (He comes from the south; the 'young fellow' is described as coming down 'from your way' i.e. from the north.)

Lyriel's answer: they passed nobody; the girl spoke of a newer grain seller; they will watch for him going south and tell him the carter is looking; the carter 'would get a better price going home full'.
Both statements (the girl's 'newer grain seller', the carter's 'young fellow... new man') are on the page; no character connects them, and Sylvanas does not mention grain as a candidate carrier.

CHAPTER 4 CONNECTS IT: the granary keeper Joss has bought from 'a new man with a cart' for three months, cheaper than the valley farms by two coppers on the measure, from the west road; four loads, the last a fortnight ago; young, civil, brown or fair, good horse, bought Joss a jug and asked after his wife's leg. Jaina thinks of the girl's 'Cheaper than Mister Hollis' at once; she and Sylvanas (who was in the doorway when the girl said it) both reach 'one new man, selling cheap at Millhaven and here.'

Chapter 4: his flour (new pale sacks stencilled with a wheat sheaf in a ring and the word ANDORHAL) is the carrier; a hidden jar of the built contamination is under the loft floor; the watcher Tam says 'I'm not to speak to you'.
Chapter 4: the cart came by the west road; Brask: Andorhal is the big granaries three days south-west; the party follows the grain road. Jaina: 'Or where he wanted us to think it came from.'

Chapter 5: the young cart man is not alone: 31 to 53 places on four roads in one season; Corley's yard books load, not man. Miller past Coldwell: a young fellow came back 'yesterday' to buy back the last four sacks of his own load at above the selling price ('the damp had got into them'); the Wick ostler: a free carter left south before light that morning, 'He always paid'. Sylvanas: someone is a day ahead every time. The cart man is one carrier; whether that miller's young fellow is Millhaven's man is not stated.

notes_chapter5: Chapter 5: no face is given; the cart man becomes one of many 'own cart' carriers. Sylvanas's belief that she was following one man collapses. A buy-back at a loss shows a cleaner-up, not a profit-maker.
readerKnows: A newer, cheaper grain seller called at the girl's house in the last days; a carter independently asks about a young new grain man.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas heard both as ordinary road gossip, unconnected. She does not link grain to the sickness. Jaina heard both; nothing on page shows her thought.
notes_chapter4: NOW CONNECTED (supersedes the Ch3 'must not be connected' caution): the newer grain seller is the carrier chain's front man. The old carter (Ch3) is NOT mentioned in Ch4 and no link between the carter and this man is stated. Hold the carter's identity and any Barov connection back (plan: not earned).
